name: Central bank stress
value: Fed Dec rise priced ~89%; BoE at 4%
summary: Markets price an 89% chance of a December Fed rate rise after hot October CPI; BoE signals another rise is likely
state: After October CPI beat forecasts on 10 Nov, CME FedWatch showed an 88.8% chance of a Fed rate rise in December, up from about 72% a week earlier, and Governor Waller said the Fed should raise rates (Yahoo Finance). Markets priced about a 66% chance of an ECB rise in December. Bank of England Deputy Governor Lombardelli said on 10 Nov that another near-term rise was likely after the 5 Nov increase to 4% (Trading Economics). Central banks face rising inflation and slowing growth; no emergency move was found.
for_you: Borrowers on variable or soon-to-renew mortgages and loans are most exposed if rates rise again. Savers tend to see deposit rates follow policy rates upwards.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma across Fed, ECB, BoE and BoJ: Watch; no emergency moves or coordinated intervention

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — Fed rate hike odds in December at 88% after hot CPI

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
